comparator.name: Bachelor Chemical Engineering and Chemistry
comparator.sourceNotes: The current 2026–2027 Chemical Engineering and Chemistry after-revision OER and appendices were freshly retrieved and inspected on 8 October 2026. All 27 required-course/project/open-space positions total 180: core 125 including 6BFR01 Bachelor Final Project 15, ITEC 10, free 45. Year one is core 60; year two core 35 + ITEC 5 + electives 20; year three taught core 15 + project 15 + ITEC 5 + electives 25. Current 6BBR03 Calculus for Chemical Engineering and Chemistry replaces older 2WCB0. Required 6CBL02 is CBL Process Technology; optional Process Dynamics and Control 6BER07, Analytical Chemistry 8BE150 and CBL Process Design 6BER11 are not universally compulsory and are not added. The current ordinary programme is English; announced 2027–2028 Dutch/English tracks do not alter current instruction metadata. PPD is embedded, MyFuture carries no extra EC and five Studium Generale activities belong within ITEC obligations. Free electives require at least 30 EC at levels 2/3 including 15 at level 3, approval and non-overlap. The ordinary three-year BEP is scheduled in quarter 4 as a block; students enrolled longer than three years may use other quarters. BEP entry requires at least 120 credits including all compulsory first-year components and at least 40 EC of post-propaedeutic core, including 6CBL01 CBL Molecules and Materials or 6CBL02 CBL Process Technology. Admission to 6CBL02 requires Physical Transport Phenomena 1 (6BPR01) and Chemical Reactors (6BPR04) each completed with at least 6, or an alternative partial-test route specified in Appendix 2; the representative curriculum includes both foundations. The interdisciplinary challenge requires prior completion of the offered units containing PPD skills. Future course admission and timetabling remain conditions; no new UCR judgment is made. Independently verified 2 November 2026: current OER SHA256 2f590b1d796f43fb11ab5bf0f25cd13a4e83b4e714f551b919a6b0e5ce56aa88, Appendix2 pp72–77 confirms all27 positions/180EC and project/practical entry rules. Completing35 post-propaedeutic core EC in year2 plus Chemical Bonding and Spectroscopy5 in year3Q1 establishes the required40 before ordinary Q4 BEP, with CBL Molecules and Materials included. No formal specialization; genuine45EC open space remains open, recommended electives not imported as requirements.

core: Biochemistry, biomolecules, cells and molecular laboratory methods
Sustainable materials, lifecycle analysis, environmental chemistry and resource recovery
Mathematics, programming, numerical methods and data analysis for material and environmental systems
Experimental research, chemical-product questions and team product development

trace: develops a product concept, fabrication method and prototype and evaluates sustainability and cost; it supports chemical-product design questions without teaching chemical synthesis or process equipment
develops actual R data preparation, visualization and a research project using chosen data; chemical or materials data are possible applications, not mandatory datasets
supplies structured programming, testing and debugging for quantitative analysis and system models
develops calculus, complex numbers, differential equations and dynamic-model implementation for quantitative scientific analysis; no dedicated linear-algebra claim
teaches stable numerical solution methods for equations, interpolation, integration and differential equations
develops probability, distributions, estimation and simulation for experimental and model uncertainty
directly investigates material composition, chemical leaching, ICP metal analysis, electrochemical recovery and laboratory yields for recycling and remediation
examines how public and private actors make and implement sustainability policy, a concrete institutional dimension of lower-impact industrial transition
uses field and laboratory analyses to study soil properties, remediation and aquifers as material and environmental systems
uses system modelling, proxies and isotope tracers to analyse linked Earth-system processes and greenhouse-gas pathways
studies aqueous and mineral biogeochemical processes, water treatment and resource recovery using geochemical modelling
conducts advanced research on resources, geothermal energy, carbon capture and waste storage
establishes physics, chemistry, materials, mathematics and modelling foundations for sustainability problems
extends the sustainability foundation through waves, chemistry and materials science in an applied project
examines climate drivers, impacts, mitigation, renewable energy and carbon storage as the context for lower-impact production
directly evaluates environmental impacts of products and processes across their lifecycle and develops circular-economy planning
assesses energy-use patterns and technically and economically evaluates solar, wind and bioenergy system designs
teaches advisor-supported research-question formulation, literature review, planning and investigation for a partner sustainability question; chemical subject matter and techniques are not guaranteed
introduces biochemistry, macromolecules, cells and DNA as a biological foundation for molecular and biotechnology questions

studies molecular mechanisms of primarily eukaryotic cells, thermodynamic free-energy calculations and critical research-method appraisal; molecular drug-target analysis supplies a health-facing application
directly studies proteins, sugars, lipids, nucleic acids, metabolic pathways and biotechnology applications
provides biochemical and molecular laboratory work with proteins, bacteria, DNA and bioinformatics
studies molecular genetics, cell injury, inflammation, repair and disease as one health-facing application of molecular science

alternatives.label: Biochemistry, environmental chemistry & sustainable resource systems
alternatives.concept: Combine biomolecular and laboratory science with environmental biogeochemistry, materials and resource recovery, lifecycle analysis, renewable systems, mathematics, programming and data methods. This is a related interdisciplinary response to evidenced biochemical and sustainable-chemistry interests, not Chemical Engineering and Chemistry equivalence.
alternatives.labelReason: The schedule contains cumulative biomolecular/laboratory and environmental-chemistry/resource strands, supported by lifecycle, quantitative and design methods; the label does not claim general, organic, physical or process chemistry depth.
progression: Current offerings and earlier formal prerequisites verified for all24 courses. PPD is in year1. Both introductory science foundations and programming precede later methodological and laboratory work. Research in a Sustainable Delta is offered only in the opening Fall: its supported role is advisor-guided formulation, literature and investigation, with techniques depending on the partner project. No prior disciplinary prerequisite or guaranteed chemical experiment is invented. Later laboratory and quantitative courses deepen the research foundation.

candidates.label: Molecular synthesis, polymers and nanoscale materials
candidates.reason: Actual biopolymer preparation/testing, copper analysis, biomolecular mechanisms, leaching/metal recovery and geochemical equilibrium are positive chemistry contributions. They do not establish a distinct complete molecular-design/synthesis, catalysis, polymer/nanoscale-characterization progression. Reusing the broad related programme would not create a substantive new direction.

candidates.label: Chemical processes, production and reaction engineering
candidates.reason: Actual recovery separations, product material balances/prototyping, numerical differential-equation methods and life-cycle assessment support process-related questions. They do not establish transport/reactor engineering, industrial chemical process design/control/safety as a separate complete programme. No missing planning coverage or title-only rejection used.

selection.assessment: One complete related-fields programme passes the academic and mechanical gates. It owns the integrated biochemical, sustainable-material, environmental-chemistry, resource and experimental interests through actual course content. A second specialist chemistry/process route cannot supply general, organic, inorganic, analytical or physical chemistry sequences; chemical thermodynamics and kinetics; polymer chemistry; molecular synthesis; catalysis; transport phenomena; reactors; separations; process control or process safety. The isolated biochemistry, environmental biogeochemistry and sustainability courses cannot be relabelled as that disciplinary formation, so no padded second programme is produced.

blocks: Biochemistry, cells and molecular laboratory work
Both introduce molecular foundations; UCR centres biomolecules, cells and DNA, while the external component also establishes chemical-process engineering.
Both directly study biochemistry and biotechnology; UCR focuses on biomolecules and metabolism and does not reproduce the external engineering context.
Both establish programming for quantitative scientific work; the external component also contains a dedicated linear-algebra strand.
Both establish calculus for later quantitative work. UCR includes differential equations and dynamic modelling, but does not reproduce the target’s specialised chemical-engineering mathematics.

notes.text: The UCR programme combines biochemistry and molecular laboratory work with environmental biogeochemistry, resource recovery, lifecycle analysis, renewable systems and quantitative methods. It does not reproduce the target’s general, organic, inorganic, analytical and physical chemistry; chemical thermodynamics and kinetics; polymers and synthesis; transport phenomena, separations, reactors, process control and safety; specialist laboratories or Chemical Engineering and Chemistry capstone.

audience.programmeDescription: TU/e Chemical Engineering and Chemistry studies molecules, materials and chemical processes, combining laboratory chemistry, mathematics and engineering with sustainable energy and health applications.
audience.comparisonExplanation: TU/e provides a dedicated chemistry and chemical-engineering formation. UCR offers a related interdisciplinary programme with actual biomolecular and environmental chemistry, material recovery laboratories, sustainable resources and quantitative methods. It does not reproduce the full synthesis, physical chemistry, polymer, transport, reactor, process-control or specialist laboratory sequence.

curriculum.routeLabel: Current English-taught programme; no formal specialization
curriculum.limitation: Recommended electives are not additional compulsory courses. Future offerings and admission conditions remain subject to the applicable regulations.

componentNotes.4CBLW00: Requires completion of previously offered components embedding communication, cooperation, planning and organization skills.
componentNotes.0LVX30: Engineering Ethics and Engineering for Society each carry 5 EC. Personal and professional development is embedded. Five Studium Generale activities and MyFuture activities totaling a value of seven are noncredit obligations.
componentNotes.cp-000270-y2-open-8: 20 EC of genuine approved open study in year 2, followed by 25 EC in year 3. At least 30 EC of the combined 45 EC must be at intermediate or advanced level, including 15 EC at advanced level; content must not overlap. Submit a complete study plan for approval after earning 90 EC.
componentNotes.6CBL02: Entry normally requires Physical Transport Phenomena 1 and Chemical Reactors each passed with a grade of at least 6; the regulations also specify partial-assessment alternatives. Both foundations precede this component in the displayed pathway.
componentNotes.6BFR01: Required 15 EC final design or research project, normally a block in quarter 4 of year 3. Entry requires 120 EC, all compulsory first-year components and 40 EC of later core including CBL Molecules and Materials or CBL Process Technology. UCR optional independent research is 15 EC outside the scheduled 180 EC. Examination Board approval is required before the project starts. Assessment includes a written thesis and an oral presentation, with individual contributions identifiable in joint work.
componentNotes.cp-000270-y3-open-5: 25 EC of genuine approved open study. Changes to the approved study plan require approval.
